**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

Section 9.9 (Audit Procedures), read with 9.8 (Records), is the only audit right binding us — Section 6.9 runs in our favour (Sanofi auditing RevMed and its subcontractors). It satisfies the playbook's material terms: mutual/reciprocal right, minimum prior written notice, a per-Calendar-Year frequency cap, a bounded look-back with waiver of earlier periods, an independent auditor of international prominence subject to our reasonable acceptance, scope limited to verifying financial reports and payments, a confidentiality wall (auditor may not disclose our Confidential Information beyond the discrepancy report), and auditing-Party cost unless underpayment exceeds a stated percentage. Critically, there is no direct or remote access to our systems — books-and-records review only — so the walk-away scenario does not arise.

Noted but not flagged: the notice, frequency, look-back and underpayment percentages are redacted ([***]), so they can't be confirmed against the preferred 30 days / once per 12 months / 5% figures; and the "unless for cause" exception to the frequency cap is customary rather than an unlimited-audit right. Worth confirming the redacted figures in the execution version, but the clause sits at or above the fallback.
